security_spec.violation_condition: When QEMU still implements the now-removed per-privilege interrupt threshold CSRs mithreshold (0xFB1) and sithreshold (0x1B1), or internally consults per-privilege thresholds instead of the unified eithreshold, after this spec PR removes them in favor of a single eithreshold that controls interrupt masking for all interrupt sources (major + external) in ACLIC mode.
security_spec.summary: Removal of mithreshold/sithreshold in favor of unified eithreshold: QEMU must stop exposing per-privilege threshold CSRs and gate all interrupt delivery (including major interrupts from CLINT) through the single eithreshold when ACLIC mode is active, otherwise guest interrupt masking is silently bypassed.

findings.finding: QEMU does not define the per-privilege interrupt threshold CSRs mithreshold (0x347) or sithreshold (0x147), nor any CSR at addresses 0xFB1/0x1B1. Grep for 'mithreshold', 'sithreshold', '0xFB1', '0x1B1', '0x347', '0x147' returned zero results in target/riscv/. The only threshold mechanism in QEMU is the standard AIA IMSIC eithreshold (ISELECT 0x72) in riscv_imsic.c, which is the page-based ISELECT mechanism, not a standalone CSR. No implementation of Smidctrl/Ssidctrl (ACLIC) extension exists in QEMU, so there are no legacy per-privilege thresholds to remove or unify.
findings.snippet: #define ISELECT_IMSIC_EITHRESHOLD          0x72  // cpu_bits.h:1038 — only threshold reference in QEMU

Number  Name         Description
(NEW) 0x347   mpistatus    Previous interrupt context
(NEW) 0x347   mithreshold  Interrupt enable threshold
(NEW) 0x348   mipreemptcfg Interrupt preemption configuration

Number  Name         Description
(NEW) 0x146   spistatus    Previous interrupt context
(NEW) 0x147   sithreshold  Interrupt enable threshold

A new WLRL M-mode CSR, mithreshold, determines the priority cutoff used to mask lower-priority interrupts... In contrast to existing threshold mechanisms in AIA, this CSR applies to major and minor interrupt identities.

findings.finding: The scountinhibit_pred change adds a CDE (Custom Data Extension) check via menvcfg.CDE before allowing S-mode scountinhibit access. This is unrelated to interrupt thresholds — it enforces a missing ISA check for the scountinhibit CSR. No threshold-related regressions introduced.

The IOMMU change adds a validation that disallows MSI page table pointer (MSIPTP) being non-OFF when the IOMMU host G-stage address translation pointer (IOHGATP) is in BARE mode. This enforces a hardware constraint (you cannot have MSI remapping without a host translation context) and is unrelated to interrupt threshold CSRs.

This is the standard AIA IMSIC per-privilege eithreshold accessed via ISELECT page mechanism (select 0x72), NOT the Smidctrl/Ssidctrl mithreshold/sithreshold CSRs. The IMSIC eithreshold is NOT in scope of the Smidctrl/Ssidctrl specification per the ACLIC spec itself which states 'The AIA eidelivery and eithreshold CSRs defined for the IMSIC are not included in the scope of Smidctrl/Ssidctrl.' This is the correct, expected implementation.

spec_citations.excerpt: The AIA eidelivery and eithreshold CSRs defined for the Incoming Message Signaled Interrupt Controller (IMSIC) are not included in the scope of Smidctrl/Ssidctrl.
